Neuroscientist Andrew Huberman returns to the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1842. Huberman teaches at Stanford and hosts his own science podcast, where he turns lab research into daily habits. Rogan's show gives him hours to range across the brain and body.

The talk centers on brain health: how sleep, light, stress, and training shape the mind over time. Huberman explains the science in plain terms and points to steps a person can test in daily life. Rogan steers him toward what works in practice, and the result is a wide, detailed tour of applied neuroscience.
podcast-joerogan-TP5W2MG8Jjs:
Physicist Sean Carroll joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 1352. Carroll is a leading voice on cosmology who also writes to defend a fully natural view of the universe. He is known for making the deepest physics clear without dumbing it down.

He and Rogan range across the big questions: why there is something rather than nothing, how time flows, and whether many worlds exist. Rogan asks the questions his audience sends him, including the spiritual ones Carroll politely resists. The episode is a lucid, patient tour of the cosmos by one of its best living guides.
podcast-tuckercarlson-8krG32pr5Js:
Author Ken joins Tucker Carlson to discuss his book on the plots against Donald Trump. The book covers the two attempts from the summer of 2024. Carlson notes that more questions than answers remain.

He asks why so few other books have tackled the subject. The guest says major outlets dropped the story too fast. They review official accounts that strike them as absurd. They also ask why Trump shut down the probes. The episode keeps a grave story alive and argues that the public still lacks a full, honest record.
podcast-tuckercarlson-4_G_rTeDjJs:
Senator JD Vance joins Tucker Carlson to discuss the border crisis and the race. Vance had risen fast from author to national figure. His calm style anchors the talk from the start.

The title names three topics: immigration, polls, and a plan to stop Trump. Vance argues that polls are built to fool voters and sap their will. He lays out a hard line on border control. Carlson presses him on how the left might still block a win. The episode gives a future vice president's case in full, in his own measured words.
